public_rationale: Marcus said that within hours of launch, people were posting the usual ridiculous errors, much as with earlier models. Bloomberg reported that in the first 24 hours, users complained that GPT-5 still made up information and stumbled on simple math and spelling. It cited GPT-5 miscounting the letter b in 'blueberry'. Futurism reported that users quickly posted garbled map labels from GPT-5's image output. These are the familiar kinds of LLM error, appearing right after a launch that promised PhD-level expertise. The plain reading of the claim holds. The comparison with 'every earlier model' is loose and not measured, so it is not tested beyond the recurrence of similar errors.
limitations: Error reports are anecdotal user tests, not a measured error rate.
Some errors involve image generation, which may use a different component from the text model.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: within hours to a day of the 7 August 2025 launch, users publicly documented basic, embarrassing errors or made-up content from GPT-5. These were the familiar kinds of LLM error seen with earlier models, despite big launch promises.
This does not require showing that GPT-5 made errors at the same rate as earlier models. Only the recurrence of familiar basic errors right after a hyped launch is tested.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous reports of GPT-5 making basic errors (simple math, spelling, made-up facts, garbled labels) posted by users within about a day of launch.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reports that early users found few or no basic errors, or that the errors circulating were not real GPT-5 outputs.
